title: On the Interpolation Effect of Score Smoothing in Diffusion Models
claim: Denoising with the exact empirical score collapses back onto training points, while a smoothed score interpolates between them along the subspace.
layout: Single vertical stack of 5 bands, top-to-bottom, side arrows label denoising paths
description: A tall vertical figure of five stacked horizontal bands, each holding four black plus-signs that mark training points on a line. The top band shows only the plus-signs, the clean empirical distribution. Below it, a band of gray gradient cones narrows upward to each point, which stands for the score field of the exact empirical score. The middle band shows green scatter clouds of noised samples around each point. Below that, a band of inverted gray cones converges toward the points, with lighter gray regions between them, which stands for the smoothed score. The bottom band shows teal dots spread along the line between the plus-signs, so the samples interpolate. A green arrow on the left labels the noising direction. On the right, a dashed green arrow points up for denoising with the empirical score, and a solid blue-green arrow points down for denoising with the smoothed score.
caption: From the noised empirical distribution ($p^{(n)}_{t_0}$; middle), denoising with the ESF ($\nabla \log p^{(n)}_t$) leads back to the empirical distribution of the training set ($p^{(n)}_{0}$; top), while using a smoothed SF (e.g. the Smoothed PL-ESF, $\hat{\vs}^{(n)}_{t, \delta_t}$; or NN-learned SF) produces a distribution that interpolates among the training set on the relevant subspace (e.g., $\hat{p}^{(n, t_0)}_0$ in the case of Smoothed PL-ESF; bottom). Definitions are given in Sections [ref] - [ref].
abstract: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable progress in various domains with an intriguing ability to produce new data that do not exist in the training set. In this work, we study the hypothesis that such creativity arises from the neural network backbone learning a smoothed version of the empirical score function, which guides the denoising dynamics to generate data points that interpolate the training data. Focusing mainly on settings where the training set lies uniformly in a one-dimensional subspace, we elucidate the interplay between score smoothing and the denoising dynamics with analytical solutions and numerical experiments, demonstrating how smoothing the score function can cause the denoised data samples to interpolate the training set along the subspace. Moreover, we present theoretical and empirical evidence that learning score functions with neural networks - either with or without explicit regularization - can naturally achieve a similar effect, including when the data belong to simple nonlinear manifolds.
